input.summary: Meridian's 228-row operational evidence base surfaces seven high-priority use cases, all blocked by unresolved foundation gaps.
covers: Governed data foundation for AI / LLM automation
sources: Tableau, Power BI, SAS analytics estates
Claims administration and pharmacy claims platforms
CRM member service and contact center telephony

story.meaning: Seven strategic use cases are identified and stakeholder-endorsed, but every one is blocked from decision grade by the same cluster of unresolved foundation gaps — no medallion architecture, no governance operating model, no identity spine.
story.observed: 228 operational evidence rows captured; 6 active, 222 candidate. 164 high-confidence and 64 medium-confidence signals span CEO, CFO, CIO, CTO, CISO, and Chief Experience Officer stakeholders. All seven use cases are in planning stage pending evidence closure.
story.matters: Without closing the lakehouse, governance, and identity gaps, Meridian cannot advance any use case to sourcing or investment decision. The portfolio is stalled at the planning gate simultaneously across all seven priorities.
story.supports: Nexus surfaces the shared blockers — medallion architecture, formal data governance, patient identity spine, AI audit trail — as the critical path. Resolving these four unlocks the entire use-case portfolio.

findings: All seven use cases share the same four foundation blockers: no certified medallion architecture, no formal data governance, no patient/member identity spine, and no AI audit trail — resolving these unlocks the full portfolio simultaneously.
CEO, CFO, CIO, and CTO are aligned on the lakehouse and AI governance priorities, but no use case has cleared its evidence gate; stakeholder intent is high, decision-grade readiness is zero.

Payment integrity and call center optimization carry the highest near-term CFO and Chief Experience Officer urgency, yet both are blocked by ungoverned SAS model lineage and uncertified transcript/intent taxonomy respectively.

FY26 AI spend governance and the AI Benefits Realization Ledger are active CFO and CIO priorities with no approved baseline or benefits ledger tie — spend is accumulating without a measurement framework.

opev → data governance operating model gap (blocks all AI/LLM use cases)

relationships.note: Operational evidence is the demand signal layer; every use case it surfaces feeds directly into the risk and relationship dimensions, where the same foundation gaps appear as blockers — creating a closed loop that Nexus must resolve before any use case can advance to a sourcing or investment event.

gaps.missing: No approved business case, baseline metrics, or benefits ledger for any use case
gaps.blocks: FY26 AI spend governance, AI Benefits Realization Ledger, and CFO investment decisions
gaps.needed: FP&A-validated baselines and signed benefits ledger tied to each use case
gaps.handoff: CFO / Finance & Value team to provide FP&A validation and usage extracts

gaps.missing: No certified medallion architecture or patient/member identity spine
gaps.blocks: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse — the prerequisite platform for four other use cases
gaps.needed: Epic Clarity medallion certification + identity spine load + AWS/Databricks foundation evidence
gaps.handoff: CIO / CTO to confirm AWS/Databricks readiness; CDAO to certify medallion design

gaps.missing: No formal data governance operating model, semantic layer, or AI audit trail
gaps.blocks: All AI/LLM automation use cases and CISO model-risk controls
gaps.needed: Governance charter, semantic ownership registry, HITL controls, and audit logging evidence
gaps.handoff: CDAO and CISO to co-own governance model; CIO to confirm tooling (Microsoft Purview / OneTrust)

gaps.missing: AHT, FCR, transfer rate, CSAT, and QA baselines absent for contact center
gaps.blocks: Call center optimization and Member Service Agent Assist Transformation
gaps.needed: Genesys / Salesforce / CRM baseline extracts with transcript governance certification
gaps.handoff: Chief Experience Officer and Contact Center Operations to provide baseline data

gaps.missing: SAS model lineage ungoverned; provider entity resolution and recovery workflows unproven
gaps.blocks: Payment integrity and leakage reduction — highest near-term CFO priority
gaps.needed: SAS lineage documentation, provider entity resolution proof, investigation and recovery workflow evidence
gaps.handoff: Health Plan Operations and Finance/Actuarial to certify SAS estate lineage and recovery tracking

evidence.name: Operational Process Evidence — Pattern Layer
evidence.facts: Seven use-case patterns confirmed at high or medium confidence: lakehouse, AI governance, call center, provider quality, cost transparency, payment integrity, automated close.
evidence.supports: Establishes the seven-use-case portfolio as the operational demand signal for Meridian's Nexus engagement.
evidence.missing: Pattern rows confirm intent; none confirm technical readiness, baseline metrics, or approved business cases.

evidence.name: CEO / Enterprise Strategy Stakeholder Interviews
evidence.facts: CEO endorses all seven use cases as promising but explicitly flags each as not decision-grade pending specific evidence closures — medallion architecture, governance model, contract digitization, and platform readiness.
evidence.supports: Confirms C-suite alignment on priorities and the shared evidence gate logic across all use cases.
evidence.missing: No approved business case, no signed baseline, no benefits ledger tie evidenced for any CEO-endorsed use case.

evidence.name: CFO / Finance & Value Stakeholder Interviews
evidence.facts: CFO flags AI Benefits Realization Ledger, payment integrity, cost transparency, and automated close as top priorities. FY26 AI spend governance is active with no approved baseline.
evidence.supports: Establishes CFO as the primary benefits-realization and spend-governance stakeholder; payment integrity is the highest near-term financial risk use case.
evidence.missing: FP&A validation, usage extracts, and benefits ledger ties are all required before any CFO-owned use case can advance.

evidence.name: CIO / CTO / CISO Stakeholder Interviews
evidence.rows: 10+ interview evidence items across CIO, CTO, CISO series
evidence.facts: CIO owns FY26 AI spend governance and platform use cases. CTO flags infrastructure readiness gaps. CISO requires AI governance and model-risk controls before any LLM use case can proceed.
evidence.supports: Confirms that platform, security, and governance readiness are co-owned across CIO, CTO, and CISO — not a single-owner decision.
evidence.missing: HITL controls, audit logging, model-risk evidence, and AWS/Databricks foundation certification are all absent.

evidence.name: Chief Experience Officer / Contact Center Stakeholder Interviews
evidence.rows: 5 interview evidence items (CXO and Contact Center series)
evidence.facts: Chief Experience Officer owns Member Service Agent Assist Transformation. Contact Center Operations owns platform and knowledge modernization. Both are blocked by absent transcript governance and uncertified intent taxonomy.
evidence.supports: Establishes member experience and contact center as a distinct evidence-closure workstream requiring Genesys, Salesforce, and CRM baseline data.
evidence.missing: AHT, FCR, transfer rate, CSAT, QA baselines, and transcript governance certification are all required before this workstream can advance.

evidence.name: Relationship and Risk Context — Shared Blocker Inventory
evidence.rows: 298 relationship rows; 249 risk rows; 12 named shared blockers
evidence.facts: The same 12 blockers — no medallion architecture, no identity spine, no governance model, no semantic layer, no AI audit trail, no data quality rules, no transcript governance, no real-time integration, no intent taxonomy, no member identity linkage, no provider contract digitization, no SAS lineage — appear across all seven use cases in both relationship and risk dimensions.
evidence.supports: Confirms that the operational evidence portfolio is not fragmented — it is a single shared foundation problem manifesting across seven use cases.
evidence.missing: No remediation owner, timeline, or sequencing plan is evidenced for any of the 12 shared blockers.
